key_concept: Étard reaction: chromyl chloride in $CS_2$ oxidises the methyl group of toluene only as far as the aldehyde, giving benzaldehyde, which can also be made by Rosenmund reduction.
steps: Toluene reacts with $CrO_2Cl_2$ in $CS_2$ to form a brown chromium complex (Étard complex). Hydrolysis with $H_3O^+$ then gives benzaldehyde, so P = $C_6H_5CHO$.
Statement (1) is false. Benzaldehyde has no $-COOH$ group, so it cannot release $CO_2$ from $NaHCO_3$ and no effervescence is seen. Benzoic acid would give effervescence.
Statement (2) is false. Benzene with $CH_3COCl$ and anhydrous $AlCl_3$ undergoes Friedel–Crafts acylation, which gives acetophenone ($C_6H_5COCH_3$), not benzaldehyde.
Statement (3) is false. A white precipitate with bromine water is the test for phenol (2,4,6-tribromophenol) or aniline. Benzaldehyde does not give it.
Statement (4) is true. Rosenmund reduction converts benzoyl chloride to benzaldehyde: $C_6H_5COCl + H_2 \xrightarrow{Pd/BaSO_4} C_6H_5CHO + HCl$.
final_answer: Option (4): Compound P is obtained by the hydrogenation of benzoyl chloride with Pd on $BaSO_4$.
why_not_others: Option (1) would be correct only if P were benzoic acid, which forms with $KMnO_4$, not $CrO_2Cl_2$. Option (2) gives acetophenone, and option (3) describes the test for phenol or aniline.
common_trap: Students assume chromyl chloride oxidises toluene all the way to benzoic acid. The Étard reaction stops at benzaldehyde.
time_saving_tip: Recall the standard routes to benzaldehyde: Étard (toluene + $CrO_2Cl_2$), Rosenmund ($C_6H_5COCl$, $Pd/BaSO_4$) and Gattermann–Koch. Then pick the option that names one of them.
